slices.title: Run page
slices.brief: Section 11 row S3 (the largest slice; the user's main complaint lives here). Build on S1 (src/projects/time.ts, Time.tsx, useNow.ts, TimeZoneToggle.tsx, LiveStatus.tsx, useResource meta; read docs/handoff/ux-s1.md for its deviations, e.g. the chip/toggle live in .run-status-row today and the TimeReferenceContext is provided in ProjectsView) and on S2 (contracts/projects/triage.ts: buildTimeline, deriveNow, deriveFocus, deriveAttention, humanizeEvent, nowResultUris, laneLines, textToString, COMMAND_CAPTION/COMMAND_LEGEND; read docs/handoff/ux-s2.md fully — its rich Text parts are rendered with S1's <Time>/formatters; its deviations correct some PRD premises, e.g. nodes are served failed, not paused, while a task error is kept). Ship: the Projects header in one 48px row on Projects routes only (App.tsx; skills routes keep their header); RunHeader (2-line facts line run-inputs-facts + Details disclosure run-details + definition chip keeping definition-changed/definition-current + the moved live chip and zone toggle, testids unchanged); NowBanner (run-now with data-situation, headline/reason/next rendered from deriveNow, fetching only nowResultUris lane results, cached per URI) + CommandBlock (numbered steps, <code> outside buttons, a Copy button whose text is exactly 'Copy' with aria-label 'Copy command' and a select-text fallback, the $PY/$RUN legend disclosure, caption 'Run these in your terminal; this viewer never changes a run.', testids now-command/copy-command); the lanes line for 2+ lanes; tabs [Run][Assignment] above the graph with the graph inside the Run tabpanel; routed Assignment (routes.ts accepts /runs/<r>/assignment, parse + build + tests); the fitted SVG graph per section 10 (dag.ts widths/gaps, width=100% + max-width, glyph aria-hidden, data-attention, selection ring, compact 3-li legend with data-executor, remove per-kind stroke colours and the pending dash override); StepsTimeline = the Steps <table> (run-node-list rows with data-node-id/data-status/data-attention, Started/Took/Attempts markers/Outcome/bar column, node-hint as caption line) + Activity (run-timeline <ol>, oldest first with remembered Newest-first toggle, controller-log toggle with count hiding PID rows by default, gap rows as text, attempt rows linking /nodes/<n>); StepStrip on node pages (sticky, run-node-list, li[data-node-id][data-status][data-attention] with <a aria-current>, horizontally scrollable at <=760px, prev/next); a full-width node area rendering today's NodeDetail (no node list column); the breadcrumb without Home, with a node crumb and the workflow title rule of 4.1 (activity.feature is not served until S5/S6, so use rules 2-3 now); the read-only info line only on /projects; document.title prefix '? ' while attention waits; focus management (selecting a node focuses its h3 tabIndex=-1, back restores focus to the Steps row); remove the keyboard hint, the empty Select-a-node panel, 'Last event: sequence N'. Styles in new src/projects/run.css. Fixtures in tests/project-workflows/fixtures/ux-run.ts (the S3 fixture list in 12.2), new tests/project-workflows/ux-run.spec.ts with scenarios run-now-banner, run-steps-timeline (including the 1440x900 fold assertion on RUN_REVIEWER_BLOCKED and the two-lane identical-failure fixture), graph-fits, assignment-routed, narrow-run, question-attention; the S3 migrations in 12.3 (clarity.spec.ts:118 loop, review.spec.ts:104-106, reviewers.spec.ts:135-136, projects.spec.ts:317-319 graphNode data-status on node URLs -> nodeListItem). You may fix bugs in contracts/projects/triage.ts found while wiring (S3 is allowed to edit it; keep tests/unit/triage.test.ts green and add tests for any change). The whole existing project-workflows suite must stay green in both phases apart from the listed migrations — run all of its spec files in both phases before committing since this slice touches every run page, and run the root skills specs graph.spec.ts and listing-refresh.spec.ts on ports 5184/3014 for the App.tsx header change. Before finishing, take screenshots of the new run page (1440x900 and 390x844) for RUN_REVIEWER_BLOCKED from your Playwright fixtures into /tmp/claude-1000/-home-agentops-dev-md-manager/541817b2-200f-49c5-b924-e4e11cf0112a/scratchpad/ux/after/s3-*.png, look at them, and fix anything visibly off (overlap, clipping, cramped spacing) — the goal is a page the user finds easy to scan.
slices.others: Slice S5 runs concurrently and owns server/**, contracts/projects/** EXCEPT triage.ts (v1.ts, examples.ts, contract.test.ts, *.schema.json, README.md) and config/; do not edit those. S5 does not touch src/**, triage.ts or any browser spec.

impl.summary:
Slice S3 (the run page) is done on `ux/s3` in three commits; the worktree is clean. The whole project-workflows suite passes: 43/43 in the worker phase and 43/43 in the candidate phase. The three root skills specs pass on ports 5184/3014 (21 tests). S5 is not merged into this tree, so the suite still needs a rerun after it lands.

**What changed on the page (all in `src/projects/` unless noted):**
- **Header:** on Projects routes the app header is one 48 px row with the title, the roots and Refresh (`src/App.tsx`, `src/App.css`); skills routes look as before. The breadcrumb has no Home, ends at the node, and names workflows by the PRD's title rule (rules 2-3). The read-only note shows only on `/projects`.
- **Run header (`RunHeader.tsx`):** two lines. Line one has the title, status, span, live chip and time-zone toggle; a long title is cut short so the chip and toggle stay beside the status. Line two is the facts line (`run-inputs-facts`), the definition chip and a Details disclosure.
- **Now banner (`NowBanner.tsx`, `CommandBlock.tsx`):** shows the situation, reason and next step from `deriveNow`. It waits until the lane results it needs have loaded; those are cached per URI and a 404 counts as absent. Each command has a Copy button whose text is exactly "Copy" (aria-label "Copy command"), and the block carries the `$PY/$RUN` legend and the one-line caption.
- **Lanes line and tabs:** a lanes line appears for runs with 2+ lanes. The Run/Assignment tabs sit above the graph and are routed (`routes.ts` accepts `/runs/<r>/assignment`).
- **Graph (`WorkflowGraph.tsx`, `dag.ts`):** fits the width. Each node has a status glyph in a corner badge, and a node waiting on the operator gets an amber ring. The per-kind stroke colours and the pending dash override are gone. The legend is three short items.
- **Steps and Activity (`StepsTimeline.tsx`, backed by the new pure `steps.ts`):** the Steps table is `run-node-list`, with start, duration, attempt marks (✗ ? ⚑ ⚒ ✓), outcome and bars on a time axis that shortens silences over 30 minutes. Activity keeps the node-less diagnosis and repair rows in view and puts PID rows behind "Controller log (n)"; it has a remembered "Newest first" toggle, gap rows as text, and attempt rows linking to `/nodes/<n>`.
- **Node pages (`StepStrip.tsx`):** a one-line run bar, a sticky step strip (one scrolling row on a phone) and the node in full width. Selecting a step focuses its heading; going back focuses its Steps row.
- **Attention:** while a question, pane or approval waits, the tab title starts with "? ". The announcer speaks only when the situation changes.
- **Styles:** in the new `run.css`.

**`triage.ts` fix found while wiring:** a blocked review's reason now names the reviewers that blocked first. The reviewers-flow fixture declares the superseded reviewer first, so the banner opened with the wrong cause. A unit test covers it.

**Fixtures and tests:**
- `fixtures/ux-run.ts` adds eight runs, each written once as raw controller records. The worker phase serves them through a small copy of the adapter's pre-B1 projection. A throwaway script found 0 differences against the real adapter's output.
- `ux-run.spec.ts` holds the six S3 scenarios. At 1440×900 the focus row ends at 870 px on the reviewer-blocked run and at 892 px on the two-lane identical-failure run (budget ≤ 900). At 390×844 the Now banner ends at 827 px.

**Screenshots and the visual pass:** screenshots are in `scratchpad/ux/after/s3-*.png`. Looking at them turned up seven problems, all fixed:
- the graph glyph collided with two-line labels;
- a paused run's bar axis ran to now, months away;
- the attempt marks were clipped;
- a repaired step showed the failure before the repair;
- the header row wrapped at 1280 px;
- step labels were cut off on a phone;
- phone tap targets were under 44 px.

The handoff is `docs/handoff/ux-s3.md`.

1. **Files outside the S3 list:** `NodeDetail.tsx` (one attribute, `tabIndex={-1}`, for focus) and the `lanes.spec.ts:250-251` migration, which PRD 12.3 missed. New `steps.ts`, `routes.test.ts` and `steps.test.ts` sit inside S3's scope but are not named in its row.
2. **Tabs on node pages:** the Run/Assignment tabs also show on node pages, because `guardrails.spec.ts:297` clicks Assignment from a node page and is not in the migration list.
3. **Warning tokens:** the `--warn-*` and `--attention` colours are defined in `run.css`, not `index.css`.
4. **No `features/viewer-ux-s3/policy.json`,** same as S1.
5. **Roots nav:** it moved inside `<header>` on every route. Skills pages look the same, but the keyboard now reaches the roots before Refresh.
6. **Breadcrumb:** the run crumb has no status glyph, because `Breadcrumbs.tsx` takes plain text labels.
7. **Status wording:**
   - `run-status-meaning` uses a new short wording (`RUN_STATUS_SHORT`); `RUN_STATUS_MEANING` stays for the list badges.
   - On a phone the header hides that phrase visually (screen readers still read it), since the banner repeats it.
8. **Run bar:** it links the Now headline back to the run page instead of showing "Next step ›".
9. **RUNBOOK:** named as text with every section in the tooltip, not linked, since the viewer cannot serve `RUNBOOK.md`.
10. **Graph:** the status glyph is a corner badge so it clears two-line labels.
11. **Activity:** the raw message and sequence number are in a tooltip, not an expander. Controller outages appear only as gap rows, not as hatched bands on the worker bars.
12. **Steps table:**
    - "Took" runs from the first start to the last verdict.
    - "Outcome" shows the step's latest status row when it is newer than the last verdict.
13. **Tab title:** it keeps the page's existing title (`md-manager`) after the `? Waiting · <run> — ` prefix.
14. **Worker-phase events:** derived from the same raw records as the seed through an in-module copy of the pre-B1 projection, checked for parity against the real adapter.

findings.summary: The candidate row's attempt marks put one mark per lane span in the same string as the attempt number, so a two-lane candidate reads as three attempts with the first one passed.
findings.failure_scenario: I ran stepRows on the real workflow-guardrails-001 payload (scratchpad ux/api). The candidate row came out as `attempt 2 · ✓✗✗`. The ✓ is lane controller's pass on attempt 1, and the two ✗ are lane ui's failures on attempts 1 and 2. Since the marks are documented as 'the marks of its attempts in time order', a reader counts three attempts and thinks the first one passed. The marks should be grouped per attempt, or per lane for the failing lane only (for example `✗✗` for ui).

findings.summary: At 760 px and below, `.run-definition { display: none }` hides the definition chip, including the `definition-changed` warning. The Details disclosure only gives the pinned revision, so on a phone nothing says the definition changed.
findings.failure_scenario: Open a run whose workflow definition changed after the run started (the lanes.spec `definition-changed` fixture) at 390×844. The 'definition … (changed since; this run keeps its own)' span is display:none. Details shows 'Pinned definition … revision X' and nothing about the current revision, so a phone reader cannot learn that this run's graph differs from the current definition. The warning chip (or the fact) should move into Details at this width instead of disappearing.

findings.summary: `buildTimeline(run)` is not memoized. It runs again on every render, which means on every 1 s `useNow` tick of a non-terminal run. `laneLines` and `deriveNow` also build their own timelines, so each poll builds the same timeline three times, against PRD 5.1's memoization on (last_sequence, inputs, review).
findings.failure_scenario: On a running or awaiting-approval run page, RunView re-renders every second because of `clock`. Each render calls `buildTimeline(run)` and `stepRows(...)`, even though `run` only changes on a 5 s poll. It is cheap on today's roughly 40-event payloads, but it scales with event count on long runs. It also leaves `useMemo` on `run` beside it that shows the intent. `useMemo(() => run && buildTimeline(run), [run])` (and passing the timeline into laneLines/deriveNow later) fixes it.

spec_gaps: PRD 10 'Graph fit': between 760 and 1,100 px the graph scrolls inside its box 'with the focus node scrolled into view'. WorkflowGraph has no scroll logic (only width 100%/minWidth 0.83), so at about 900 px a focus node such as review or integrate starts off-screen in the box. This gap is not listed among the deviations.
PRD 11/12.2: the scenario ids are not recorded in features/viewer-ux-s3/policy.json (acknowledged deviation 4).
PRD 4.2/5.2 rule 6: controller outages are not drawn as hatched bands on overlapping worker bars (acknowledged).
PRD 5.3: the Activity sequence number and full message sit in a title tooltip, not an expander (acknowledged). A tooltip is not reachable by keyboard or on touch.
PRD 3.2/4.2: the run crumb has no status glyph ('skeleton-001 ✗') (acknowledged).
PRD 4.4: the node-page run bar has no 'Next step ›'; the headline links back to the run page instead (acknowledged).
PRD 10: the --warn-*/--attention tokens are defined in run.css, not index.css (acknowledged).
PRD 6.4: the tab title reads '? Waiting · <run> — md-manager', not '… — MD Manager', because it keeps the existing document title (acknowledged).
PRD 12.2 graph-fits says 'Guardrails bounding boxes stay in x-order'. The test uses the single-lane RUN_GUARDED, so the x-order of stacked two-lane columns is not exercised.
PRD 12.2 question-attention asks for 'a banner with both answer forms naming the lane' in that scenario. It checks only the first command (the second form is asserted in run-now-banner instead).
review.notes:
I reviewed `git diff feature/viewer-ux..ux/s3` (3 commits) against PRD_VIEWER_UX sections 3-12. No P0-P2 defects, three P3 findings.

**Checks re-run in the worktree:**
- The four unit files: 103/103 pass.
- `tsc -b`: clean.
- eslint on the changed files: clean.
- I did not re-run Playwright; the implementer reports 43/43 in both phases.

**Probe on the captured payloads:** a scratch script (`scratchpad/rev-s3/probe.ts`) ran `stepRows`, `deriveNow` and `laneLines` on skeleton-001, skeleton-fixes-001 and workflow-guardrails-001.
- skeleton-001 matches the PRD wireframe: challenge `?✗✓` 11m07s, worker 28m21s from the receipts, verify `✗✗⚑⚒✓` 10m02s, candidate ≈1m06s, review ≈2m10s, `review_blocked`, run end 09:32:31.
- skeleton-fixes-001 gives `succeeded`.
- Guardrails gives the two lane lines. It falls to `check_failed` only because the scratchpad has no `candidate_ui/1` (the real server serves it).
- The one oddity is the candidate marks `✓✗✗` (finding 1).

**Traced and found correct:**
- **Result cache:** keys are absolute run-scoped URIs, so runs cannot collide. A 404 counts as absent, and failed fetches retry on Refresh.
- **Title and announcer:** `RunView` is keyed per run, so the `document.title` cleanup and the announcer's "speak only on a situation change" state are per run.
- **Focus:**
  - Selecting a step focuses the h3 (`tabIndex -1`, `preventScroll`), and going back focuses the step's row.
  - The requirement-highlight flow survives the new `scrollTo(0,0)` because TaskPanel uses `keepInView`.
- **Routes:** `routes.ts` rejects `/assignment/<x>` and keeps every existing URL.
- **Pinned wording kept:** `did not complete`, `not complete`, `Viewing does not approve it` and `Read-only`.
- **Legend:** three `li[data-executor]` items, as the clarity spec pins.
- **No execution controls:** the only new buttons are Copy, More/Less, Newest first and Controller log (n). Commands sit in `<code>` outside any button, so `expectNoExecutionControls` still passes.
- **Spec migrations:** the 12.3 S3 migrations are done. The extra lanes.spec change is justified: the graph and `inputs-none` are no longer on node pages.
- **Red evidence:** it came from assertions failing against skeleton exports, not from compile errors. The new spec assertions can fail: the graph-fits red measured scrollWidth 1688 > 1212.

**Design notes, not defects:**
- The worker-phase fixture carries about 25 lines copying the pre-B1 `normalizeEvents` projection. Nothing enforces parity with the adapter, so it will drift once S5/B1 lands. The implementer already flags a rerun after S5.
- `useRunResults` keeps a module-level cache of up to 200 entries across pages, which works but departs from PRD 7's run-scoped `useRunData`. That is planned for S4-core.

outcomes.item: P3 src/projects/steps.ts:62 candidate attempt marks one per lane span
outcomes.note: Confirmed ('✓✗✗' on guardrails). steps.ts attemptMarks now groups spans by attempt: running if any lane is live, else the worst lane verdict. The guardrails candidate now reads 'attempt 2 · ✗✗'. A new unit test was red first.

Confirmed. Only the definition-current chip is hidden now (.run-definition:not(.projects-warning)). The narrow-run scenario asserts definition-changed is visible at 390px on run-succeeded; it failed first with 'hidden'.

Smaller than reported: buildTimeline already caches per run (keyed on last_sequence, statuses, inputs, review, results), so deriveNow and laneLines hit that cache and never rebuilt it. Each clock tick only paid the key check. It is now useMemo on run, with a comment. stepRows stays per tick because a running step's duration grows.

outcomes.note: WorkflowGraph takes a focusId prop (RunView passes the Now focus) and centres the focus node in its scroll box when it starts outside; only the box scrolls. graph-fits asserts it at 780px on run-awaiting-approval. It was red first: approval started outside the box.

outcomes.note: Deviation 4 stands, as in S1's deviation 10: a policy.json on its own would make a malformed feature directory. The ids are listed in the handoff.

Unit tests on the guardrails payload (4m56s and 6m35s on both workers, none on other steps) were red first. No browser fixture has an outage inside a worker span, which is noted as a follow-up.

outcomes.item: gap: Activity seq/full message in title tooltip, not expander
outcomes.note: A row that rewords its message has a '#n' button (activity-more, aria-expanded, aria-controls) that shows the served message under the row (activity-raw). run-steps-timeline opens it with the keyboard. It was red first.

outcomes.item: gap: run crumb has no status glyph
outcomes.note: Deviation 6 stands. Breadcrumbs.tsx is in src/graph, outside S3's files, and takes plain-string labels, so a bare ✗ would be read aloud. The header status badge sits directly below the crumb.

outcomes.item: gap: node-page run bar lacks 'Next step ›'
outcomes.note: Deviation 8 stands. The sticky step strip directly below the run bar has Next › and Prev, and the headline links back to the run page.

outcomes.item: gap: --warn-*/--attention tokens in run.css not index.css
outcomes.note: Deviation 3 stands. index.css is outside S3's file list, and the tokens are defined for both colour schemes. The handoff proposes a PRD correction.

outcomes.item: gap: tab title suffix 'md-manager' not 'MD Manager'
outcomes.note: Deviation 16 stands. The prefix keeps the page's existing title, which is index.html's static <title>md-manager</title>, outside S3's files.

outcomes.item: gap: graph-fits x-order not exercised on two lanes
outcomes.note: Test only. graph-fits now checks on the two-lane run-succeeded that the launches share one x, the verifications share one x, and the seven columns are strictly increasing. It passed immediately, so the product was already correct.
